questions.question: Snails is an example of which of the phylum of animal kingdom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mollusca**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mollusca:-**

 
 
• **Molluscs are characterized by their soft bodies, which are often protected by a hard shell. **
 
• They also have a unique digestive system that includes a muscular foot, a radula (a tongue-like organ with rows of teeth), and a gizzard. 
 
• Molluscs are divided into several classes, including the Gastropoda (snails and slugs), Bivalvia (clams and oysters), Cephalopoda (squids, octopuses, and nautiluses), and Polyplacophora (chitons).
 
• **Snails are an example of the phylum Mollusca.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Arthropoda:-**

 
 
• **It is the largest phylum in the animal kingdom, comprising about 80% of all known animal species. **
 
• Arthropods live in all habitats on Earth, from the sea to the air, and from the poles to the tropics.
 
 
 
• **Protochordates:-**
 
 
• **These are an informal category of animals that are closely related to vertebrates. **
 
• They are invertebrates, but they share many of the same characteristics as vertebrates, such as a notochord (a flexible rod that runs along the back of the animal), a dorsal nerve cord, and pharyngeal gill slits.
 
 
 
• **Annelida:-**
 
 
• **It is a phylum of segmented worms, with over 22,000 extant species including ragworms, earthworms, and leeches. **
 
• The species exist in and have adapted to various ecologies – some in marine environments as distinct as tidal zones and hydrothermal vents, others in fresh water, and yet others in moist terrestrial environments.

questions.question: Mallika Sarabhai was awarded with Padma Bhushan (2010) - for contirbution to Performing Arts. She was highly recognized for which dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mallika Sarabhai:-**

 
 
• **Mallika Sarabhai is an Indian Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer, stage actress, director, and social activist.**
 
• She is the daughter of dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai and prominent space scientist Vikram Sarabhai.
 
• Sarabhai began learning dance from her mother at the age of 5.
 
• She emerged as a professional dancer in the 1970s and has since performed all over the world. She has excelled in both Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam.
 
• Sarabhai is also active as a stage actress.
 
• She has acted in several plays and films, including Peter Brook's play Mahabharata in the role of Draupadi.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatanatyam**:

 
 
• Bharatanatyam is the oldest of the classical Indian dances, and is said to have originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is a highly expressive dance form that combines complex footwork with graceful arm movements.
 
 
 
• **Kathak**:
 
 
• Kathak is a northern Indian classical dance that is known for its storytelling elements.
 
• It is often performed to the accompaniment of Hindustani classical music.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali**:
 
 
• Kathakali is a traditional dance form from Kerala that is known for its elaborate costumes and makeup.
 
• It is typically performed by men and tells stories from Hindu mythology.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi**:
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a classical dance from Andhra Pradesh that is known for its dynamic movements and expressive gestures.
 
• It is often performed to the accompaniment of Telugu classical music.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri**:
 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance from the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• It is known for its graceful movements and fluid transitions.
 
• It is often performed to the accompaniment of Manipuri folk music.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**:
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance from the eastern Indian state of Odisha.
 
• It is known for its sculpturesque poses and fluid movements.
 
• It is often performed to the accompaniment of Odissi classical music.

questions.question: Which of the following dance is particular to the women of the Kamad tribe?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Garai dance**__**.**

__
 
• **Garai dance**

 
 
• **It is a folk dance performed by the Kamar tribe in Madhya Pradesh, India. (Hence, option 4 is correct)**
 
• It is a vigorous and energetic dance that is performed by women.
 
• The dancers sit on the ground and tie cymbals to different parts of their body, including their legs, hands, and head.
 
• They also balance a sword in their teeth and an ornamental pot on their head. 
 
• The Garai dance is a ritualistic dance that is performed to worship Baba Ramdeo, a folk deity who is believed to have lived around the beginning of the 16th century.
 
• The dancers sing songs in praise of Baba Ramdeo and his miracles. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhutia dance:-**

 
 
• **It is a traditional dance form of the Bhutia people, who are an ethnic group found in Sikkim, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, and other parts of India, Bhutan, and Nepal.**
 
• Bhutia dance is a vibrant and energetic dance form that is performed to celebrate festivals, religious ceremonies, and other special occasions. 
 
 
 
• **Garai dance:-**
 
 
• **Garai dance is a traditional dance form of the Tripuri people, who are an ethnic group found in the state of Tripura in India.**
 
• Garai dance is a vibrant and energetic dance form that is performed to celebrate festivals, religious ceremonies, and other special occasions.

questions.question: "Goitre" is a disease of which of the following glands?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thyroid gland .**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goiter:-**

 
 
• **It can be caused by a variety of factors, including iodine deficiency, autoimmune diseases, and inflammation. **
 
• Goiters can be harmless, but in some cases they can cause symptoms such as difficulty breathing or swallowing, and they may also be associated with thyroid hormone problems.
 
• **Goiter is a disease of the thyroid gland.**
 
 
 
• **​Thyroid Gland:-​​**
 
 
• ​The thyroid is a butterfly-shaped gland located in the neck just below the Adam's apple.
 
• It produces hormones that control many bodily functions, including metabolism, heart rate, body temperature, and mood. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Pituitary gland:-**

 
 
• It is a small, pea-shaped gland located at the base of the brain.
 
• It is often called the "master gland" because it produces hormones that regulate many other glands and bodily functions.
 
 
 
• **Pancreas:-**
 
 
• It is a long, flat gland located behind the stomach.
 
• It has two main functions: to produce digestive enzymes and to produce hormones.
 
 
 
• **Adrenal Glands:-**
 
 
• These are two small glands located above the kidneys.
 
• They produce hormones that help the body to respond to stress and to regulate blood sugar levels.

questions.question: Which of the following is an agro-based industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sugar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Agro-based industries:-**

 
 
• **These are those that use agricultural products as their raw materials to produce a wide range of goods and services. **
 
• These industries play a vital role in the economy, providing employment and income to millions of people, and contributing to food security and export earnings.
 
• Agro-based industries can be further classified into two categories:
 
 
• **Primary agro-based industries**: These industries process agricultural products into basic products, such as flour,** sugar, **and oil. **(Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• **Secondary agro-based industries:** These industries process basic agricultural products into more sophisticated products, such as bread, biscuits, and confectionery.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mineral-based industries:-**

 
 
• **These are industries that use minerals and metals as raw materials to produce finished goods. **
 
• These industries are essential to the global economy, as they provide the materials needed for a wide range of products, from construction materials to electronics.
 
• **Aluminium, iron, steel, and coal are not agro-based industries. They are mineral-based industries, which means that they use minerals as their raw materials.**
 
 
• Aluminium is produced from bauxite ore, which is a mineral.
 
• Iron and steel are produced from iron ore, which is also a mineral.
 
• Coal is a fossil fuel, which is formed from the remains of ancient plants and animals.

questions.question: What is the currency of Bangladesh, a neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**taka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Taka:-**

 
 
• **It is the official currency of Bangladesh. **
 
• It is subdivided into 100 poisha.
 
• The taka was introduced in 1972, after the independence of Bangladesh from Pakistan.
 
• The currency is issued by the Bangladesh Bank.
 
• The taka is a symbol of Bangladesh's national identity and economic progress.
 
• It is also a reminder of the country's struggle for independence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kyat:-**

 
 
• **It is the official currency of Myanmar (Burma). **
 
• It is subdivided into 100 pyas. The kyat was introduced in 1952, after the independence of Myanmar from the British Empire.
 
• The currency is issued by the Central Bank of Myanmar.
 
 
 
• **Ngultrum (BTN):-**
 
 
• **It is the official currency of Bhutan. **
 
• It is subdivided into 100 chetrums.
 
• The ngultrum was introduced in 1974, and it is currently pegged to the Indian rupee at par.
 
 
 
• **Yuan:-**
 
 
• **It is the official currency of the People's Republic of China (PRC).**
 
• It is the basic unit of the renminbi (RMB), which literally means "people's currency".

questions.question: Under which amendment act, article 51A (k) of the Indian constitution was inserted in the constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eighty - sixth amendment Act**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A(k):-**

 
 
• **It was inserted in the Constitution by the 86th Amendment Act, of 2002. **
 
• It is a fundamental duty of every citizen of India, who is a parent or guardian, to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years.
 
 
 
• **(Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002:-**
 
 
• The 86th amendment act was inserted as 21A in article 21 in 2002, which tells about the right to education.
 
• It became the fundamental right for children between 6-14 years.
 
• As per this amendment, the state shall provide free and compulsory education to 6 to 14 years in such a manner as the state may by law determine.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eighty-second Amendment Act:-**

 
 
• It amended Article 16(4) of the Constitution to allow for the relaxation of qualifying marks and standards of evaluation in matters of reservation in promotion for members of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **Eighty-first Amendment Act**
 
 
• It amended Article 16(4A) of the Constitution to allow for the carry forward of unfilled reserved vacancies for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes from one year to the next.
 
 
 
• **Eighty-fourth Amendment Act:-**
 
 
• This amendment froze the constituency boundaries for the Lok Sabha and the Legislative Assemblies of the States until the first census after 2026, and refixed the number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes on the basis of the 1991 census.

questions.question: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio was a teacher of which college in 1820s?

• He was a radical thinker of his time and one of the first Indian educators to disseminate Western learning and science among the young men of Bengal. 
 
• He was educated at the Anglo-Indian College, where he excelled in his studies. 
 
• **After graduating, he was appointed as a teacher at Hindu College. (Hence option 1 is correct)**
 
 
 
• **Hindu College, Calcutta:-**
 
 
• It is an educational institution in the city of Kolkata, West Bengal, India.
 
• **It was founded on 20 January 1817 and is one of the oldest colleges in India.**
 
• Hindu College played a vital role in the spread and promotion of modern education in India during the British Raj.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **It was founded in 1919 by Bharat Ratna Mahamana Pandit Madan Mohan Malviya, the founder of Banaras Hindu University (BHU). **

• **Indian Institute of Science Bangalore:-**

• **The institute was established in 1909 with active support from Jamsetji Tata and thus is also locally known as the "Tata Institute".**
 
• It was granted a deemed university status in 1958 and recognized as an Institute of Eminence in 2018.

questions.question: The upper portion of the mantle is called ____________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**asthenosphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asthenosphere:-**

 
 
• The upper portion of the mantle is called the asthenosphere (astheno means weak). (Hence option 1 is correct).
 
• It lies just below the crust extending up to 80-200 km.
 
• It is highly viscous, mechanically weak and ductile and its density is higher than that of the crust.
 
• These properties of the asthenosphere aid in plate tectonic movement and isostatic adjustments (the elevated part at one part of the crust area is counterbalanced by a depressed part at another).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Mesosphere:

 
 
• The mesosphere is the layer of the atmosphere where the shooting stars blaze.
 
• It is extended from 50 km to 80 km above the earth's surface.
 
• The space debris begins to burn up as it enters the mesosphere.
 
 
 
• **Barosphere:-**
 
 
• It is the part of an atmosphere below the exosphere.
 
• **It is the region of the atmosphere where the air pressure is high enough to support life. **
 
• The barosphere extends from the Earth's surface to an altitude of about 100 kilometers (62 miles).
 
 
 
• **Lithosphere:-**
 
 
• **It is the rigid, outermost shell of a terrestrial planet or natural satellite. **
 
• On Earth, it is composed of the crust and the lithospheric mantle, the topmost portion of the upper mantle that behaves elastically on time scales of up to thousands of years or more.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc946d2bceb2a062dbac62800db09d1917e1c951b6529055f8a86a303bcca49f.png]

questions.question: After the victory over Sakas, who among the following adopted the title of 'Vikramaditya'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta II:-

 
 
• One of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta II, also known by his given name Vikramaditya and Chandragupta Vikramaditya. **(Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• He was the third ruler of the Gupta Empire in India.
 
• The famous Chandragupta II was the child of Samudragupta and Datta Devi.
 
• The Gupta empire was extended by Chandragupta II to the western sea coast, a vital area for trade and commerce.
 
• As a result, Malwa and Ujjain (Ujjayini), the region's capital, enjoyed prosperity.
 
• The second capital of Chandragupta II was Ujjayini.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chandragupta I (319AD-334 AD):

 
 
• He was the first Gupta ruler to assume the title of *Maharajadhiraja*.
 
• He strengthened his kingdom by the matrimonial alliance with the powerful family of Lichchhavis, who were the rulers of Mithila.
 
• He got married to the Lichchhavi princess *Kumaradevi*.
 
• He started the Gupta Era in 319AD-320 AD.
 
• He established his authority over Magadha, Saketa and Prayaga.
 
 
 
• **Skandagupta:-**
 
 
• Skanda Gupta also took the title Vikramaditya.
 
• Skandagupta was the last powerful Gupta Monarch.
 
• He took the title of Maharajadhiraja.
 
• Bhitari pillar depicts the information about Skandagupta of the Gupta Empire.
 
 
 
• Kumaragupta I:-
 
 
• ​He was the son and successor of Chandragupta II.
 
• Kumaragupta I's reign was marked by peace and relative inactivity, which was a result of the stability and prosperity achieved during the reign of his father, Chandragupta II.

questions.question: The materials, through which things can be seen, are called _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**transparent materials.**__​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transparent Materials:-**

 
 
• **The materials, through which things can be seen, are called transparent materials.**
 
• Transparent materials allow light to pass through them completely without scattering it. This is why we can see objects clearly through them.
 
• Some examples of transparent materials are:
 
 
• Glass
 
• Water
 
• Air
 
• Clear plastic
 
• Diamonds
 
 
 
• **Transparent materials are used in a variety of applications, such as eyeglasses, windows, lenses, and telescopes.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Opaque materials:-**

 
 
• The materials are those that do not allow light to pass through them. When light strikes an opaque material, it is either absorbed or reflected. This is why we cannot see through opaque materials.
 
 
 
• **Translucent materials:-**
 
 
• These are those that allow light to pass through them, but scatter it in a way that objects behind the material are not clearly visible.
 
• This creates a unique visual effect that can be used in a wide variety of applications, from architecture to fashion.
 
 
 
• **Conductive materials:-**
 
 
• These are those that allow electricity to flow through them. This is because they have a large number of free electrons that can move around and carry the electric current.

questions.question: As of 2022, who is the India's last living Sadhir dancer honoured with Padma Shri Award in 2022?

questions.question: The Gram Sabha is a meeting of all adults who live in the area covered by a __________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**panchayat.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Panchayat:-**

 
• **It refers to the system of local self-government in rural India. **
 
• It is a three-tier system consisting of gram panchayats at the village level, panchayat samitis at the block level, and zilla parishads at the district level.
 
• Panchayats are elected bodies, with members directly elected by the people of the area. They have a wide range of functions, including:
 
 
• **Providing basic services such as drinking water, sanitation, and roads**
 
• **Promoting economic development and employment**
 
• **Protecting the environment and natural resources

 Upholding social justice and equality**
 
 
 
• The Panchayati Raj system was enshrined in the Indian Constitution by the 73rd Amendment Act of 1992. This amendment gave panchayats constitutional status and guaranteed them certain powers and functions.
 
• **The Gram Sabha is a meeting of all adults who live in the area covered by a panchayat.**

questions.question: Which freedom fighter of British India is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Syed Ahmed Khan.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Syed Ahmed Khan:-**__

 __
 
• He was a Muslim scholar, social reformer, and educationalist in British India.
 
• He was one of the first Muslim intellectuals to argue that Hindus and Muslims were two distinct nations with different cultures and values.
 
• He believed that Muslims could not prosper in a united India dominated by Hindus, and that they needed a separate homeland where they could practice their religion and culture freely.
 
• **He is widely regarded as the "father of the two-nation theory". (Hence option 2 is correct)**
 
• Khan's two-nation theory was later adopted by the Muslim League, led by Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
 
• The Muslim League campaigned for the creation of a separate Muslim state in British India, which eventually led to the partition of India and the creation of Pakistan in 1947.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru:-**

 
 
• He was an Indian anti-colonial nationalist, secular humanist, social democrat, and author who was a central figure in India during the middle of the 20th century.
 
• **Nehru was a principal leader of the Indian nationalist movement in the 1930s and 1940s. Upon India's independence in 1947, he served as the country's first prime minister for 17 years. **
 
• Nehru promoted parliamentary democracy, secularism, and science and technology during the 1950s, powerfully influencing India's arc as a modern nation.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:-**
 
 
• **He was one of the pioneers of the Indian independence movement. He is considered the "Father of Indian Unrest" by the British.**
 
• Tilak was a staunch nationalist and believed that India should be independent from British rule.
 
• He was a leading figure in the Swadeshi movement, which promoted the use of Indian-made goods instead of British goods.
 
• He also founded the Home Rule League, which demanded self-government for India.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Ali Jinnah:-**
 
 
• **He was a Pakistani barrister, politician and statesman who is widely regarded as the founder of Pakistan.**
 
• Jinnah was initially a member of the Indian National Congress (INC), but he became disillusioned with the party's secular policies. He believed that Muslims needed their own political party to represent their interests.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: Which act was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal in the year 1773?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Regulating Act.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Regulating Act:-**

 
 
• The Regulating Act was passed by the British Parliament in 1773.
 
• **The Act was designed to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India and to curb its powers.**
 
• It was the first major intervention by the British government in the affairs of the East India Company and paved the way for further reforms and acts.
 
• The Act established a system of governance in India, with a Governor-General and a Supreme Council, and also introduced other reforms such as the establishment of a court of justice in Calcutta.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Government of India Act:-**

 
 
• The Government of India Act is a set of laws passed by the British Parliament between 1773 and 1935 to regulate the government of India.
 
• **The Government of India Act 1935 was a landmark piece of legislation that introduced a number of important constitutional reforms in India, including:**
 
 
• The establishment of a federal system of government, with a central government and provincial governments.
 
• The introduction of direct elections to the provincial legislatures.
 
• The expansion of the franchise to include more Indians.
 
• The creation of a Federal Court, with the power to adjudicate on disputes between the central government and the provincial governments.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act:-**
 
 
• The Indian Councils Act was a series of laws passed by the British Parliament between 1861 and 1909 to expand the size and functions of the legislative councils in British India.
 
• **These acts were introduced in response to growing demands for self-government from Indian nationalists.**
 
 
 
• **Charter Act:-**
 
 
• A Charter Act is a law passed by the British Parliament to renew the charter of the British East India Company, which was a private company that ruled British India on behalf of the British Crown.
 
• **The Charter Acts were passed every 20 years, and they regulated the company's trade and administrative powers.**

questions.question: The grading system used by the Mughals to fix rank, salary and military responsibilities is called ___________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mansabdari system.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mansabdari system:-**

 
 
• ​The Mansabdari system was introduced by Akbar for military administration and for the territorial command to sustain the parts of the army.
 
• The Mansabdari system was taken from the system followed in Mongolia.
 
• The Mughal officers whether Hindus or Muslims were given territorial commands in return for military service.
 
• They had to bring in some fixed number of men-at-arms, horses, and elephants to the field and were rated as per the numbers which were known as Zats. 
 
• 'Zat' shows the number of troops that a mansabdar was expected to maintain, while 'sawar' indicate the actual number of horses under the command of a mansabdar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Iqta system:-**

 
 
• The Iqta system was provided institutional status by Iltutmish__.
 
• The Iqta System or Iqtadari System was introduced by Shamsuddin Iltutmish of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• It was a powerful instrument for centralization.
 
• It was based on the division of territories between Sultans and Nobility.
 
 
 
• **​Ryotwari system:-**
 
 
• Ryotwari System was introduced by Thomas Munro in 1820.
 
• First Ryotwari System was introduced in Madras.
 
• The principle was the direct collection of land revenue from each individual cultivator by government agents.
 
• The advantages of this system were the elimination of middlemen, 
 
• In this system, the Individual cultivator is called Ryot.
 
• This system was in operation for nearly 5 years.
 
 
 
• **Mahalwari system:-**
 
 
• The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1822 by Holt Mackenzie.
 
• Later, the system was reformed during the period of William Bentick in 1833.
 
• **This system divided the land into Mahals. Sometimes, a Mahal was constituted by one or more villages.**
